La Clause 46 des CCG n’indique que les principes de base et les restrictions générales, sans entrer dans le détail des critères de fixation et de paiement des montants à reverser. For Tender Actions of lower value, the use of ECOS is an optional choice, unless differently indicated in the specific Conditions to Tender or price requirements. Even when the use of ECOS is not mandatory, the ESA Industrial Audit Office and the ESA Cost Engineering Section highly recommend the use of ECOS for the preparation of a compliant price proposal. In all cases where the bidder decides not to use ECOS, the price breakdown presentation shall respect the format of the PBF. For this reason, a template of the PBF is available as MS Excel file and published in esa - star. PRICE CONDITIONS The price conditions are normally part of the costing requirements published by ESA, or by the issuing entity in cases on non - ESA Tender Actions. Price type and economic conditions The price type refers to the definitions included in the ESA/REG/002 Annex II. In case of Firm and Fixed Price (FFP) and Ceiling Price to be converted to Firm and Fixed Price (CP - >FFP), the price shall cover the inflation of prices over the planned full duration of the contract. The term ‘Firm’ means that no adjustment for price inflation can be done after the signature of the contract. The term ‘Fixed’ means that no adjustmen t of the price can be done as result of the actual cost incurred. In case of Fixed Price with price Variation (FPV) the cost shall respect the required economic conditions (i.e. the overall state of economy in the Country of the bidder at a given year and month; e.g. 07/2025) and therefore the financial inflation shall not be included. This type of price represents a risk sharing scheme on financial inflation: a formula bas ed on inflation indices is agreed in advance and used to compensate the general inflation of prices. The cost rate shall be comprehensive of direct costs (i.e. salaries and social charges), as well as any direct (e.g. other personnel costs) and indirect (e.g. General & Administration) overheads; this combination is referred to as ‘gross rate’. Productive hours Bidders shall refer to the ESA definition of productive hours : the normal number of hours that direct personnel record to funded and partially funded activities, including any self - funded R&D. The word ‘normal’ refers to the requirement that the rates and overheads allocated to each unit of production shall not be significantly influenced as a consequence of a particular economic situation, abnormal production, uncommon practices or idle facilit ies/personnel. In essence, for the calculation of the productive hours, the bidder shall consider an optimal production level. The following tasks are excluded from productive hours : Proposals and Tenders, Training, internal general meetings, administrative, management and other non - productive time. It is expected in general that the average productive hours are within 75 - 95% of the average worked hours. Worked hours are related to the personnel work conditions and exclude any sort of absence.
